chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Baḥr, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:

The Imams are at the rank of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, except that they are not Prophets, and it is not permissible for them regarding women what was permissible for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. As for whatever is apart from that, then in it they are at the rank of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women, in the context of marital legal permissions
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams, the divinely designated leaders
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: at the rank or status of

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the rank of the Imams in relation to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imams occupy a rank analogous to that of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in matters other than Prophethood and certain exclusive legal permissions. It affirms the exalted station of the Imams while explicitly denying Prophethood for them, preserving the distinction between Imamate and nubuwwah.
